propositions: The generic reads-under-sync-contention property does not subsume the original CLI show regression test because fault seeds F3 (empty but shape-valid JSON) and F6 (missing ticket_id field) are caught only by the original test's content-completeness assertion, not by the generic property's shape-only validation.

Reverting the actual slim-fetch-ledge fix leaves both burst tests green; only the deterministic held-lock tests detect the original regression, proving the storm test does not reliably protect against the bug it is named for.
The generic property catches fault classes (F5 stall, F7 empty list output) that the original test misses, confirming neither test subsumes the other and both remain necessary complements.
Fault-seeded detection matrix establishes by mutation-score criterion (Just et al. FSE 2014) that removing either test decreases detection coverage, licensing neither deletion.
Runtime overlap alone does not prove test redundancy; formal subsumption requires equivalent mutation detection, which this ticket disproves via seven independently seeded defects.
